procedural_matters: NZL 5 represented by Brendon Hogg Witnesses; Philippe Mazard and Lauren Twigg Jury members
facts: Second upwind, top third of the leg, NZL 5 on port tack.
Jury boat facing downwind ahead of NZL 5, slightly to leeward
Jury boat was slowly reversing to avoid an unidentified boat that suddenly tacked onto port, resulting in the jury boat being on a converging course with NZL 5.
1 boat length away from the reversing jury boat, NZL 5 bore away to pass to leeward of it
Jury boat then accelerated forward causing NZL 5 to further bear away
NZL 5 ended up port side parallel to starboard side of jury boat
After the jury boat further accelerated they cleared NZL 5, who returned to close-hauled course
NZL 5 lost 6 places as a result of the incident
conclusions: The second change in direction of the jury boat, which caused NZL 5 to take further avoiding action and sail away from her proper course, was an improper action of the Protest Committee.
NZL 5's place in race 5 was made significantly worse through no fault of her own, by an improper action of the protest committee. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b) (1) are met.
decision: Redress is given to NZL 5. NZL 5 is to be scored 65 points in race 5.
